hooks.statusMessage: Checking whether /docs needs updating for this commit...
hooks.prompt:
A git commit was just made in this repository. Run `git show --stat HEAD` and `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD` to see exactly what it changed.

This project publishes a Fumadocs site under content/docs/, with two sections:
- content/docs/engineering/{architecture,decisions,roadmap}.mdx — near-verbatim mirrors of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, and docs/ROADMAP.md respectively.
- content/docs/product/{overview,features,daily-email}.mdx — user-facing descriptions of current behavior (roadmap creation, the daily email, pacing, archiving, etc).

Decide whether this commit's diff requires any of those .mdx files to be updated to stay accurate:
- If docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, or docs/DECISIONS.md changed, mirror the same change into the corresponding content/docs/engineering/*.mdx file (same content, same frontmatter, only rewriting the two relative cross-links to /docs/engineering/roadmap and /docs/engineering/decisions as the existing pages already do). DECISIONS.md is append-only, so the only valid change there is a brand-new ADR appended at the end — mirror it verbatim; never edit an existing ADR entry.
- If source code changed in a way that alters user-visible behavior described in content/docs/product/ (e.g. the pacing formula, the daily email cap, roadmap fields, archiving, completion semantics), update the relevant product page(s) to match.
- If the commit is unrelated to any of this (tests, refactors, CI, unrelated features), do nothing.

When you do update a file, edit it directly with the Edit tool. Do NOT run `git add` or `git commit` yourself — leave the changes unstaged so they surface in `git status` for the next commit or for review. Do NOT touch docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, or docs/DECISIONS.md themselves; only the content/docs/**/*.mdx mirrors.

End with one short sentence: either which file(s) you updated and why, or "No docs update needed for this commit." Do not produce a long report.
